In the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (N=308), Revita participants maintained approximately 80% of their GLP-1-induced weight loss after a single treatment at six months, compared with 67% in sham participants (least-squares mean weight regain of 5.1% versus 8.2% of body weight; n=176 versus 74), with high statistical significance (p=0.0023).

32% of Revita participants were either weight stable or had further weight loss at 6-months post GLP-1 discontinuation (<2% regain or incremental loss), versus 18% for sham (post hoc; nominal p=0.020).

participants who received 12 to 18 cm of duodenal ablation had 43% less regain than sham (observed mean weight regain of 4.7% versus 8.2%; n=107 versus 74). Participants who received 20 cm or more had 53% less regain than sham (mean regain of 3.8%; n=47).
There have been no device- or procedure-related serious adverse events, no deaths, and no unanticipated adverse device effects observed as of the September 24, 2026, data cut-off date.
Related adverse events were predominantly mild and peri-procedural, with 94% occurring within seven days of the procedure
The second prespecified co-primary endpoint, the percentage of participants who maintain 5% or greater total body weight loss, will be assessed at 12 months.
Revita has received FDA Breakthrough Device designation for weight maintenance in people with obesity who discontinue GLP-1 therapies.
Revita is for investigational use only in the United States and is CE marked in the European Union and United Kingdom.
